title: Qwen3.6-27B unsloth GGUF with the MTP head intact (llama.cpp)
slug_note: A GGUF that keeps the MTP draft head, so llama.cpp can spec-decode the dense 27B.

variation.quant_detail: GGUF retaining the MTP head for llama.cpp speculative decoding
variation.revision_note: HF snapshot of unsloth/Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-GGUF resolved and served on the Spark during the 2026-10-27 test

engine.config: llama.cpp with --speculative-type or draft from the MTP head, per repo notes

requirements.notes: Measured on a DGX Spark (2026-10-27): 20.1 GiB dropped from MemAvailable with the recipe as written (llama-server build 11866 (commit 3f03b1772), --ctx-size 8192). Earlier estimate: Resident estimate from the quant size plus KV headroom.

steps.text: Install a current llama.cpp build with CUDA for NVIDIA or Metal for Apple Silicon, following the model card's platform-specific instructions.
The source notes MTP does not yet support multiple parallel slots or --mmproj; remove -np 1 only after checking the current engine docs.

measurements.method: openai_bench.py: streaming /v1/chat/completions, single stream, one warm-up discarded, fresh nonce per summarise prompt (cold prefill), decode = (completion_tokens-1)/(last-first token time), temperature 0.6, median of 3; summarise neutral filler (630-token prompt, 256-512 output tokens)

drop in MemAvailable from before start (OS file cache dropped) to server ready; llama-server build 11866 (commit 3f03b1772), --ctx-size 8192

caveats: No numbers yet; the forum's vLLM MTP=3 rows for this model show ~2x, llama.cpp's gain is unmeasured here.

Works as written on a DGX Spark (2026-10-27): `llama-server -hf unsloth/Qwen3.6-27B-MTP-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL -ngl 99 -c 8192 -fa on -np 1 --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 2` — llama.cpp build 11866 (commit 3f03b1772); server ready 20 s after start with the OS file cache dropped; the functional check passed; MemAvailable dropped 20.1 GiB (weights + KV at --ctx-size 8192).
